lead.title: Ambrose (UK) acquires AM-Pharma (Netherlands) for up to €161M for its enzyme ilofotase alfa in adult hypophosphatasia
lead.deck: The British rare-disease acquirer, which picks up stalled molecules that already have human data, adds a third asset: an enzyme replacement therapy ready for Phase 2 in adult-onset hypophosphatasia (HPP), where no approved treatment exists. The total includes commercial milestones and royalties; the upfront is undisclosed.

milestone.title: Roche drops RG6540, the allogeneic CAR-T inherited from Poseida, less than two years after the deal worth up to $1.5B
milestone.summary: The off-the-shelf CD19/CD20 candidate was removed from the Phase 1 pipeline on October 22; the lupus trial was withdrawn in August and the B-cell cancer trial terminated. Roche keeps other CD19/CD20 candidates from Poseida that it considers "superior", and up to $472M in contingent payments remain unresolved.
milestone.why: A signal on how hard allogeneic cells are in autoimmunity (persistence): worth keeping in mind before backing off-the-shelf CAR-Ts, and a reminder that an acquisition exit does not erase clinical risk.

brefsEurope.title: Verdiva ends its Phase 2 weight-maintenance study of the weekly oral GLP-1 VRB-101
brefsEurope.summary: The ClinicalTrials.gov record (NCT07553299) lists the study as terminated for a "business decision", not for safety; according to trade press, only 8 of 120 planned patients were enrolled. Verdiva, launched in 2025 with a $410M Series A, continues developing VRB-101 as a standalone treatment.

brefsIntl.title: Sanofi exercises its option on a first oral immunology candidate from its Recursion collaboration
brefsIntl.summary: The milestone triggers $10M; Sanofi will lead development with Phase 1 planned for 2027, and Recursion can still receive more than $300M in milestones plus royalties. The target and indication are undisclosed.

word.definition: T cells from healthy donors, engineered to target the disease, manufactured in batches and stored frozen, instead of being made to order from each patient's own cells.

parts.label: Donor cells
parts.role: raw material shared across many patients

parts.label: CAR receptor
parts.role: the antenna that recognizes the target (e.g. CD19, CD20)

how.t: T cells from a healthy donor are collected and edited to remove the receptor that would attack the patient.
The cells receive the CAR, are expanded and frozen: a single production run serves many doses.
The thawed dose is infused with no waiting time; the clinical challenge is how long the cells persist against the patient's immune system.

word.why: The promise is lower cost and speed versus autologous CAR-Ts, but persistence remains the hard part: Roche just dropped RG6540 (ex-Poseida) just as allogeneic cells target autoimmunity. For a VC, it is an editing-platform bet, sensitive to durability data.
